newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open softer in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open softer in mixed trade.

text.p: Australian shares were softer at the opening on Friday with no guidance from a holidaying New York market and ahead of local balance of payments data.
The All Ordinaries index was down 3.0 points at 2,383.3 in early trading.
Opening trade was a mixed bag, with strength in National Australia Bank battling weakness in bellwether BHP.
The rest of the leaders little changed.
"It's very quiet with Wall Street closed last night," said broker Tony Russell of Morgan Stockbroking, suggesting the market was likely to wander in the absence of clear signals.
"I think it is probably just drifting down," he said.

Turnover figures topping the A$1 billion (US$810 million) mark belied modest activity as the trading statistics were boosted by the exercise of options after the November series options expired on Thursday.
National Australia Bank was the earl star, jumping to record highs after announcing a A$1.1 billion share buyback.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio if about 14 to 13, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
